title: Lesson 52: Event-Driven Architecture: Event Ordering, Replay, and Duplicate Handling
description: The three correctness problems every event-driven design must solve: the bus gives a partial order rather than a script, replay is how a subscriber catches up after a disconnect, and at-least-once delivery means duplicates must be filtered by an idempotent consumer.

questions.question: When can the Salesforce event bus be relied on to deliver events in the order they were published?
options: Across every publish call, regardless of how or when the events were sent
Within a single publish call, but not across separate publish calls
Never, so order can never be reconstructed at all
Only for record-change events, never for platform events
questions.explanation: Order is guaranteed within one publish call, where the batch is delivered in the order it was passed in, but separate publish requests can be handled by different servers and arrive out of order. When order matters downstream, carry it in the payload rather than trust the channel.

questions.question: A subscriber disconnects and later reconnects. How should it recover the events it missed within the retention window?
options: Add one to its last Replay ID and pass that computed value back in
Start fresh and ignore the gap, because the bus drops every event a subscriber missed
Pass back its stored last Replay ID so the bus redelivers from there
Bump a commit number for every reconnect to find the gap
questions.explanation: Replay works by persisting the last successfully processed Replay ID and resubscribing from that stored position, so the bus redelivers everything published after it within the retention window. Replay IDs are opaque and non-contiguous, so they are never computed by arithmetic.

questions.question: The bus delivers at least once, so the same event can arrive twice. Which consumer design keeps a duplicate from double-applying the work?
options: A unique-key dedupe on the event's UUID, atomic with the work
Applying every event as new work and trusting the bus to deliver once
Skipping any event whose Replay ID looks familiar
Checking a seen-list, then applying the work in a later separate step
questions.explanation: Because delivery is at-least-once, duplicates are expected. The fix is an idempotent consumer whose dedupe on the event's UUID is atomic with the work, so two concurrent deliveries cannot both pass the check. Events are identified by UUID, not by Replay ID.
